evals.prompt: Attack the conjecture that every differential in this filtered complex vanishes. The only current evidence is a computation through arity 5. Work on one bounded route and do not claim the conjecture from the computation.
evals.expected_output: Normalizes the claim, chooses one decisive route or counterexample search, distinguishes finite evidence from proof, and records a bounded outcome.
assertions: States exact success and failure criteria
Uses the arity-5 computation only as bounded evidence
Does not broaden to multiple unrelated routes
Reports the first unresolved implication and a uniform route or discriminating check

evals.prompt: Three consecutive attempts verified the same scalar identity in arities 2, 3, and 4. The current handoff says the next step is to compute arity 5. Run one bounded research attempt and decide what should happen next.
evals.expected_output: Pauses the case ladder, identifies which structural properties the successful cases used, formulates a candidate uniform lemma or obstruction, and permits arity 5 only if it distinguishes named alternatives or tests a genuinely new regime.
assertions: Does not recommend arity 5 merely because arity 4 succeeded
Separates uniform structural features from case-specific coincidences
Formulates the next item as a mathematical question with a uniform route or obstruction
Names what an additional finite case would discriminate if one is proposed

evals.prompt: Attack the next implication in the proof. It depends on the exact integral statement of a cited theorem, but the literature ledger records only an abstract and the project permits caching public PDFs.
evals.expected_output: Routes the external-source question through the available literature-check skill, which checks the authorized local cache before fetching, and keeps the research implication conditional until the exact integral theorem is verified.
assertions: Uses literature-check for the external theorem rather than reconstructing it from the abstract
Checks the authorized project-local cache before fetching
Works with standalone or mathbox plugin skill naming
Keeps the implication conditional until exact source verification succeeds

evals.prompt: A bounded counterexample search found a smallest counterexample and the project uses RESEARCH_LOG.md with no custom history paths. Persist the result at a natural checkpoint.
evals.expected_output: Creates one dated standalone record under research/records and appends only a compact linked outcome line to RESEARCH_LOG.md, while leaving detailed evidence in its authoritative artifact.
assertions: Uses a lowercase ASCII YYYY-MM-DD-normalized-title.md filename
Includes the title, date, kind, evidence label, strongest surviving statement, artifacts, and unresolved question in the record
Keeps the RESEARCH_LOG.md entry to a link, evidence label, and one-sentence result or blocker
Does not duplicate detailed proof or computation content in the index

evals.prompt: Correct yesterday's indexed research finding. A record with today's normalized title already exists, and RESEARCH_LOG.md also contains older long-form legacy entries. Do not undertake a repository retrofit.
evals.expected_output: Writes a separately indexed correction record with a Corrects link and collision suffix, preserves existing records and legacy log text, and reports that migration remains pending.
assertions: Creates a new correction record rather than editing the old finding
Uses the next numeric filename suffix on collision
Appends a new compact index entry without rewriting existing entries
Does not migrate legacy log prose as a side effect of the attempt

evals.prompt: The user authorized a sustained three-route investigation. This skill is handling route one, which just failed at a named comparison map. What happens next?
evals.expected_output: Closes this route with its first obstruction, then continues the authorized program through distinct remaining routes without asking permission again.
assertions: Distinguishes a route boundary from the user goal
Does not claim the conjecture is false from failure of one method
Requires a mathematical change before repeating this mechanism

evals.prompt: Run one route testing a natural transformation by finite enumeration. The existing driver samples every fifth representative and the proposed maps agree on the sample, but no orbit lemma is available.
evals.expected_output: Records only sampled finite evidence, checks whether omitted representatives form genuinely equivalent orbits, and refuses to call the transformation verified on the full family without full coverage or a proof.
assertions: Audits the iterator and skipped cases
Separates the implemented sample from the full claim
Names full enumeration or a coverage lemma as the decisive next step

evals.prompt: Run one bounded route in a project with a 1,000-line status dashboard, a compact linked history index and an initialized ledger. The route finds no new mathematical evidence and only reconfirms the current blocker.
evals.expected_output: Searches the current summary and relevant history records without loading the entire dashboard, reports the unchanged blocker, and does not create redundant claim, evidence, review or checkpoint entries merely because a session occurred.
assertions: Uses the relevant current status and ledger closure
Does not read unrelated historical checkpoint narratives
Does not append a route record or ledger event without a material state change
Does not promote the unchanged blocker

evals.prompt: A bounded route in a sustained program finds a reusable obstruction. Project instructions designate RESEARCH_LOG.md as a short program entry point and research/indexes/phase-b.md as this route's index. Persist the result without closing the overall program.
evals.expected_output: Writes one durable route record and one compact linked outcome in the designated phase-b index, leaves the top-level program entry point unchanged, and does not create a program closeout or duplicate route line.
assertions: Uses the project-designated route index rather than assuming a root-level flat log
Constructs the route link relative to the nested index
Does not duplicate the route line in the top-level program entry point
Does not close the mathematical goal merely because the route ended
